stack.frontend: Simple web dashboard (React/Next.js) for merchant onboarding, invoice entry/import, status view
stack.backend: Node.js or Python (FastAPI) service handling UBL 2.1 XML generation, cryptographic stamping/signing and calls to ZATCA Fatoora API
stack.database: PostgreSQL (e.g. via Supabase) for merchants, invoices, CSID credentials, audit logs
stack.authentication: Simple email/password or Supabase Auth for clinic/merchant staff logins; per-merchant ZATCA CSID/PCSID credentials stored securely
stack.ai: Optional: Claude/GPT API for Arabic support chatbot or OCR-based invoice data extraction from photos/paper invoices (not required for core compliance MVP)
stack.apis: ZATCA Fatoora Compliance CSID/OTP API and Invoice Reporting/Clearance API (UBL 2.1 XML, XAdES signing, QR code, cryptographic stamp) — public docs at zatca.gov.sa
stack.hosting: AWS/DigitalOcean (region near KSA, e.g. Bahrain, as no confirmed KSA-only hosting requirement found this session)
stack.payments: Moyasar or Tap for merchant subscription billing (KSA-native gateways)
stack.integrations: Optional WhatsApp Business/Cloud API (via BSP e.g. 360dialog/Twilio) for Arabic-language notifications and support

mvp_scope: Merchant onboarding wizard: collect VAT/CR details, run ZATCA OTP + Compliance CSID setup
Manual invoice entry or CSV import UI, auto-generate UBL 2.1 XML + cryptographic stamp + QR code
Real-time submission to ZATCA clearance (B2B) / reporting (B2C) endpoints with success/error feedback
Basic Arabic dashboard + invoice history/status log
Flat monthly subscription billing via Moyasar/Tap
results.monthly_run_cost_sar: ~150-400 SAR (hosting + optional WhatsApp BSP fee + payment gateway base fee)

regulatory.requirement: ZATCA Phase 2 e-invoicing technical compliance: UBL 2.1 XML, cryptographic stamp, QR code, real-time clearance/reporting via Fatoora API; solution must pass Compliance CSID technical checks (six mandated technical capabilities per aggregator summaries)
Saudi PDPL: merchant/customer invoice data is personal data requiring lawful basis and technical/organizational safeguards; administrative penalties up to SAR 5 million for violations

data_dependencies: ZATCA Fatoora sandbox/production API access and per-merchant OTP/CSID onboarding
Ongoing tracking of ZATCA wave/schema changes (spec evolves — 'build once' is not sufficient; requires continuous compliance engineering)
Merchant's own transactional/invoice data, provided directly by the merchant (not publicly available)
blockers: High liability exposure: a bug in XML generation, stamping, or submission timing could cause the CUSTOMER to be fined (SAR 5,000-50,000 per violation per candidate's own evidence) or face VAT suspension — solo founder has no legal/E&O insurance budget to absorb this risk

Crowded, better-resourced competitive field already serving SMEs (Wafeq, Qoyod, Daftra, Sowaan, InvoiceQ, Zatify) — several are established companies with existing ZATCA integration track records, raising customer-acquisition difficulty for a new solo entrant
Requires continuous maintenance as ZATCA updates schemas/waves — not a 'ship once' MVP, ongoing compliance-engineering burden for one person

Standard commercial registration is very likely needed to sell compliance SaaS to Saudi VAT-registered businesses and to be a reachable/accountable party — no specific URL verified this session for this requirement, but it is a near-certain prerequisite
results.summary: Technically the core build (XML generation, cryptographic stamping, ZATCA API calls, simple onboarding UI) is achievable by a solo founder using AI coding tools in 6-10 weeks and does not require any paid ZATCA certification fee — ZATCA's own guidance indicates compliance is judged per taxpayer via Compliance CSID rather than requiring the software vendor itself to be pre-approved (per aggregator summaries of zatca.gov.sa). However this sits in a HARD-complexity, regulated-data category because (a) errors directly cause customer financial/legal harm (documented penalty ranges in the candidate's own evidence), (b) ZATCA specs change over waves requiring ongoing upkeep, and (c) the market already has multiple funded/established competitors. Feasible to build, but the liability and competitive-moat questions (not the coding) are the real risk for a single founder.

mvp_scope: Clinic staff dashboard to add/edit appointment slots and patient phone numbers
Automated WhatsApp reminder templates sent 24h and 2h before appointment
Patient reply-based confirm/cancel via WhatsApp webhook, updating the dashboard
results.monthly_run_cost_sar: ~100-350 SAR (hosting + WhatsApp per-message fees at small volume [~SAR 0.04/utility msg] + optional BSP platform fee + payment gateway base)

regulatory.requirement: Saudi PDPL: patient contact/appointment data linked to a clinic context is treated as sensitive personal data, requiring explicit informed consent and enhanced security/accountability measures
WhatsApp Business Platform requires Meta business verification and pre-approved message templates before sending reminder ('utility'/'marketing' category) messages

data_dependencies: WhatsApp Business/Cloud API access — requires Meta business verification, which can add days-to-weeks of onboarding friction
Clinic-provided patient appointment/contact data (not public; must be supplied by each clinic customer)
Actual pricing of local competitors Snad/Yolo.clinic — not confirmed with a verified price page in this session
blockers: Meta's WhatsApp Business verification and template-approval process is outside founder's control and can delay launch/onboarding of each new clinic by days to weeks
At least one local competitor (Yolo.clinic, per search snippet) reportedly offers a free tier, which could undercut a paid micro-SaaS on price for the smallest clinics
Per-message WhatsApp costs plus BSP markup mean unit economics must be modeled carefully at scale, though at small clinic volumes this is inexpensive
results.summary: This is a straightforward CRUD + WhatsApp-notification integration solvable by a solo founder in 4-6 weeks using Claude Code and either Meta's direct Cloud API (cheaper) or a BSP (easier onboarding, added monthly fee). Costs are modest and within/near the stated 500-1000 SAR MVP budget. The main friction points are not code complexity but (a) Meta's business-verification/template-approval process, which is outside the founder's control, and (b) Saudi PDPL's stricter rules for health-adjacent personal data, requiring an explicit-consent flow and reasonable security practices — manageable for a solo founder but adds a non-trivial compliance checklist item beyond pure feature-building.

General knowledge (not verified via search in this session) is that free, high-quality prayer-time apps are widely available in Saudi Arabia/the Gulf, which — if true — would make a 20 SAR/month paywall on a commodity feature very hard to sell; this specific claim is NOT verified with a session URL and is flagged as HYPOTHESIS, not fact
results.summary: From a pure build-feasibility standpoint this is trivially EASY: a solo founder could ship a location-based prayer-time app with push notifications and app-store billing in 1-2 weeks for a few hundred SAR (mainly Apple/Google developer account fees). However, feasibility of BUILDING is not the problem here — the candidate provides zero pain evidence, zero payment evidence, and explicitly flags its own core weakness ('would anyone pay when free apps exist'). This candidate should not be treated as a validated opportunity; it fails the evidence-discipline and golden-rule bars this system is built on, independent of how easy the MVP would be to build. NO RELIABLE EVIDENCE FOUND for willingness to pay.
